# FRAZIL test signal layers

FRAZIL separates test material by the question it answers:

1. **Layer A — Mathematical / Unit Inputs**: generated directly by unit and
   property tests for gain mapping, smoothing, routing laws, event boundaries,
   and other exact fixtures. These are not required to be WAV files.
2. **Layer B — Engineering Diagnostic Corpus**: the ten deterministic
   `TESTDATA-001` reference WAVs in `testdata/input/`. Each filename and
   manifest entry names one primary DSP measurement objective.
3. **Layer C — Algorithm-specific Generated Probes**: reusable in-memory
   generators in [`tools/signal_generators.py`](../tools/signal_generators.py).
   Water/Ice experiments may render these to temporary files with their own
   sample rate, seed, and parameter contract; probes are not committed here.
4. **Layer D — Representative Listening Corpus**: future licensed musical material in
   [`testdata/listening/`](listening/). It supports product listening review and
   is deliberately separate from byte-exact engineering regression.

`testdata/input/` therefore means **canonical engineering reference inputs**,
not every possible test input. The current corpus is:

| Signal | Definition and primary use |
|---|---|
| `zero_input__silence.wav` | Exact digital silence for zero-input stability, DC, finite-output, event-gating, and tail checks |
| `zero_state_response__impulse.wav` | 250 ms pre-silence, one -6 dBFS impulse, and >=3 s post-silence for zero-state, latency, modal, and tail checks |
| `frequency_response__log_sweep.wav` | 20 Hz–18 kHz logarithmic sweep at -18 dBFS for frequency-dependent diagnostics |
| `harmonic_response__stepped_sine_1khz.wav` | 1 kHz windows at -36/-24/-12/-6 dBFS with exact silence gaps for level and harmonic checks |
| `intermodulation_response__two_tone.wav` | 997 Hz + 1499 Hz two-tone at -18 dBFS for nonlinear mixing and IMD checks |
| `broadband_response__white_noise.wav` | Per-signal-seeded uniform white noise near -18 dBFS RMS, with no LFO or filtering |
| `envelope_response__gated_sine.wav` | 440 Hz high- and low-level gates separated by exact silence for envelope and threshold checks |
| `transient_response__pitch_decay.wav` | Four phase-accumulated downward 180 Hz -> 55 Hz transients at documented levels |
| `aliasing_response__high_frequency_sine.wav` | Sine at `0.22 * sampleRate` for high-frequency and aliasing checks |
| `stereo_isolation__channel_probe.wav` | Left-only then right-only sine windows with exact-zero inactive channels |

All canonical WAVs are generated by [`tools/generate_testdata.py`](../tools/generate_testdata.py)
with generator version 3 and base seed `20260908`. The committed corpus is
48 kHz, stereo, `PCM_S24LE`, and kept directly in Git under the repository MIT
license. Temporary 44.1 kHz and 96 kHz variants are supported by the same CLI
but are not committed. Per-signal durations, mathematical parameters, expected
properties, analysis windows, and target tests are generated into manifest v2.

Regenerate and audit the corpus from the repository root:

```powershell
python tools/generate_testdata.py
python tools/verify_testdata.py
python tools/test_testdata.py
```

The regression test regenerates the complete corpus in a temporary directory,
compares manifest semantics, then compares each WAV byte-for-byte and by
SHA-256. It also runs standard-library semantic checks for all ten signals and
temporary 44.1/48/96 kHz generation. The verifier checks schema, diagnostic
signal metadata, provenance, MIT license, redistribution terms, PCM24 WAV
metadata, storage policy, hashes, and strict two-way manifest/`input/*.wav`
set consistency. The ignored `testdata/rendered/` directory is reserved for
generated render output and is never part of the canonical corpus.

Real musical material must not be added to `testdata/input/`. See
[`testdata/listening/README.md`](listening/README.md) for the separate license
and review contract.
